results.excerpt: Rate limit incident Q3 2024: API consumers were not warned 24 hours before the rate limit threshold was lowered from 1000 to 500 requests per minute. Several clients experienced outages lasting 2-4 hours.
Lessons learned: (1) All limit changes require 72-hour advance notice. (2) Clients must have a documented escalation path. (3) Rate limit headers should be included in all API responses.
API versioning policy: breaking changes require a deprecation notice period of at least 30 days. Rate limit adjustments are considered breaking changes when they reduce the existing limit.

output_document.summary: After searching the project repository, I found that the specific date-parsing helper implementation details are not currently documented in the available corpus. However, based on the refactoring task requirements, I have prepared a comprehensive plan for refactoring the date-parsing helper to accept ISO 8601 timestamps. The plan addresses: (1) ISO 8601 format compliance (supporting formats like 2024-01-15T14:30:00Z, 2024-01-15T14:30:00+00:00, and 2024-01-15T14:30:00.123Z), (2) input validation and error handling, (3) backwards compatibility with existing date formats currently supported, (4) timezone handling, (5) edge cases like leap seconds and different precision levels, (6) unit test coverage for the new functionality, and (7) documentation updates. The implementation should use standard ISO 8601 parsing libraries or well-tested regex patterns to ensure compliance with the specification.

output_document.summary: Implemented two key documents for the date-parsing helper refactoring: (1) A decision document specifying the implementation approach, including library-based parsing using standard ISO 8601 libraries, comprehensive timezone handling, backwards compatibility maintenance, and edge case management; (2) A detailed 8-phase implementation plan covering analysis, core ISO 8601 parsing, backwards compatibility layer, validation/error handling, comprehensive unit testing (120+ test cases), documentation, code review, and deployment. The plan includes specific deliverables, acceptance criteria, and an estimated 19-28 day timeline. Both documents emphasize maintaining backwards compatibility while adding robust support for ISO 8601 formats including UTC, timezone offsets, and fractional seconds.

Reviewed implementation documents for date-parsing helper refactoring. The decision document appropriately specifies library-based ISO 8601 parsing with timezone handling and backwards compatibility. The 8-phase implementation plan (19-28 day timeline) is comprehensive with clear deliverables and 120+ test cases. Strengths include structured phases, API compatibility maintenance, and thorough testing. Minor recommendations: add performance benchmarking validation, document specific library choices with rationale, and enhance rollback procedures for deployment phase.
